page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.2xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. A key hardware characteristic is its massive bundled local storage, consisting of 23,622 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the compute and memory subsystems operate primarily in the lower performance tiers. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmarks, along with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, fall into the bottom 25% category. Memory read bandwidth is also weak, though large-block memory write bandwidth reaches average levels. Cryptographic and compression tasks show poor to weak performance, with single-threaded gzip compression in the bottom 10%. Database operations, such as Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are similarly constrained within the bottom 25%.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.d1.2xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for scenarios requiring massive local storage capacity without the premium cost of SSDs. However, the tradeoff is significant: compute-intensive or latency-sensitive applications will be bottlenecked by the legacy HDD storage medium and the lower-tier CPU and memory performance. Consequently, this server type is best suited for storage-heavy workloads, distributed file systems, cold data archiving, and large-scale sequential data processing where storage volume is prioritized over high-speed IOPS or raw compute power.
